y1-skills: Both develop academic writing, source evaluation, research questions and responsible inquiry; UCR combines these skills with personal and community development rather than a dedicated GPM skills course.
y1-stats: Both develop introductory statistical analysis for empirical research. UCR also includes research design and a team project, without the GPM-specific applications.
y1-earth: Both address physical Earth processes relevant to environmental questions; UCR gives particular attention to geology and geological field observation.
y1-mapping: Both address spatial data and mapping. UCR develops ArcGIS analysis and remote-sensing methods for environmental inquiry.
y1-project: Both apply research to a local environment. UCR teams investigate a partner-supplied delta sustainability question, rather than the specified GPM living-environment project.
y2-qual: Both develop qualitative research design, evidence collection and interpretation for social inquiry; UCR is not specifically a geographic fieldwork course.
y2-quant: Both use statistical modelling and empirical analysis; UCR specialises in econometric estimators, tests and an empirical paper.
y2-economy: Both examine economic mechanisms relevant to globalisation and sustainability. UCR introduces markets and macroeconomics without the dedicated urban-economic framing.
y2-global: Open-economy macroeconomics addresses an identifiable economic part of globalisation; UCR does not reproduce the integrated human-geographic study of globalising places.
y2-intervention: Both examine how to intervene in sustainability problems. UCR develops governance diagnosis, stakeholder appraisal and policy advice, without reproducing the full GPM intervention-method sequence.
y3-borders: European integration and its political institutions are a substantive part of both courses. UCR examines representation, legitimacy and EU policymaking rather than a specialist geography of borders and identities.

externalBlanks.y1-intro: Selected social sciences, environmental study and spatial engineering do not supply the integrated introductory disciplinary survey of geography, planning and environment.
externalBlanks.y1-methods: UCR offers substantive statistics, qualitative methods and applied projects, shown against their strongest counterparts. No remaining selected course establishes this separate GPM research-methodology foundation.
externalBlanks.y1-spatial: Spatial engineering and nature-based interventions do not establish this component’s primary historical and social explanation of spatial transformations.
externalBlanks.y1-city: No selected course centres on competing perspectives on cities and their urban development. General sociology and comparative politics remain complementary.
externalBlanks.y1-theory: General social theory does not establish this dedicated theoretical treatment of space and environment.
externalBlanks.y2-field: Local and geological fieldwork do not reproduce the required GPM project with research during a foreign excursion.
externalBlanks.y2-migration: Introductory sociology includes migration among several topics, but does not establish a course centred on migration and social integration.
externalBlanks.y2-urban-econ: Public economics and open-economy macroeconomics do not establish sustained study of European cities, inter-city competition and urban economic geography.
externalBlanks.y2-approaches: Selected courses provide social and environmental theories, but no sufficiently direct counterpart to this integrated spatial and environmental approaches course.
externalBlanks.y2-theorising: Social theory and empirical environmental analysis do not establish the component’s specific spatial and environmental theorising function.
externalBlanks.y3-practice: Applied spatial engineering does not by itself establish the dedicated application of spatial theories in this theory-sequence culmination.
externalBlanks.y3-electives: Genuine open elective space has no predetermined substantive counterpart.
externalBlanks.y3-thesis: The selected team project is already aligned to local applied research. No scheduled course provides the individual 18-EC GPM thesis; optional independent research is shown separately under the standard comparison rule.

finding: Every fixed UCR row and every24externalcomponent reconsidered. PPD academic skills and EU integration are meaningful partial relations, statistics placed against its strongest counterpart. Migration as an incidental introductory topic and spatial engineering as a substitute for geographic theory remain insufficient. No equivalence asserted.

presentation: Default counselor comparison mode; complete selected Globalisation curriculum, two UCR alternatives. Record/content review only; no app code changed, no runtime or screenshots claimed.

audience.programmeDescription: Geography, Planning and Environment examines how people shape places and how social, economic and environmental processes interact. This comparison follows the Globalisation route, alongside shared theory, methods, fieldwork and an independent thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR programme combines global social change, public decisions, GIS, spatial engineering and applied environmental research. The other concentrates on environmental science, water, energy and sustainability transitions. Both offer relevant academic study with different specialist priorities. They do not reproduce Radboud’s dedicated geographic theory, urban planning, specialist migration and border studies, required fieldwork abroad or 18-EC individual geography thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The selected route totals 180 EC: 60 EC in each year, including 30 EC of open study and an 18-EC thesis. Thesis entry requires the named academic-skills, methodology and statistics requirements and at least 120 programme EC. Fieldwork abroad is required; destinations vary. An internship and geography teacher training are optional choices, not compulsory parts of this pathway.

componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 18-EC individual research thesis. Entry requires academic skills, methodology, statistics and at least 120 programme EC.
componentNotes.y3-electives: 30 EC of open bachelor study, normally 24 EC in the first semester and 6 EC in period three. A permitted 12-EC internship can form part of this space. External courses require approval and must avoid overlap.
componentNotes.y2-field: Required 6-EC research project with fieldwork abroad and a personal contribution. Tallinn and Bilbao are past examples, not guaranteed destinations.
componentNotes.y2-intervention: Required 6-EC course with an attendance condition.

concepts: A programme on people, environments and global change combining social theory, global economics and politics with environmental change, geospatial analysis, spatial engineering and sustainability governance. Applied delta research connects evidence to local questions; the programme does not reproduce a full human-geography or urban-planning curriculum.

A distinct environmental-science and sustainability pathway through Earth systems, climate, ecology, coastal hazards, water governance, renewable energy, circularity and applied delta research, with social research and civil-society study. It does not reproduce the Radboud dedicated spatial-planning and urbanisation curriculum.

notes.text: UCR combines relevant social sciences, environmental science, GIS, spatial engineering and delta research. Radboud GPM supplies a dedicated geographic and planning sequence, foreign fieldwork and an individual geography thesis. The alternatives offer related academic paths with important differences in specialist depth and research structure.
